newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria seeks manager or buyer for Biochim bank.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria seeks manager or buyer for Biochim bank.

text.p: Bulgaria will seek a new foreign partner to manage or take a stake in Biochim Bank after talks on a management contract with ABN AMRO NV failed, a Bank Consolidation Company (BCC) official said.
"After negotiations for a management contract with ABN AMRO bank failed, the BCC should seek alternatives to solve Biochim's management problems," the BCC board member told Reuters.
By the end of the week the BCC plans to send letters to 25 potential strategic investors offering negotiations on a management contract or privatisation deal for Biochim Bank.
On Monday, July 7 the Dutch bank said that it had no plans to seek a contract to manage Biochim bank.

So far the Dutch bank's international consultancy group has had a "twinning" relationship with Biochim Bank, under which the two banks co-operate but ABN AMRO has no management responsibility. The BCC official said he hoped that relationship could be continued.
The BCC, which manages state equity in commercial banks and holds some 98 percent in Biochim Bank, is expected to approve a package of stabilisation measures for Biochim on Friday.
In March, the government introduced a $50 million stabilisation package aimed at boosting Biochim's capital to risk assets ratio and liquidity.
Part of the scheme proposed that the finance ministry purchase long-term bad loan bonds from Biochim at par value of $100. Some $20 million of bonds were bought.
The BCC now estimates that Biochim needs around $15 million to cover its "capital gap", which could be reduced through state support and revaluation of assets, BCC figures showed.
Under pledges to the International Monetary Fund, Bulgaria should seal privatisation deals or management contracts for two of its operating state-owned banks by end-September.
The United Bulgarian Bank privatisation is awaiting a final approval by the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development board, the BCC official said.
The EBRD will take 35 percent, Bulgaria's Bulbank will take 35 percent and the U.S. Oppenheimer & Co will take the remaining 30 percent.
